sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā vālisūnur abhāṣata jāmbavatpramukhān sarvān anujñāpya mahākapīn
english: Having heard those words, the son of Vālin addressed them all — having taken leave of Jāmbavān and the great monkeys who stood foremost among them.

sanskrit: asminn evaṃgate kārye bhavatāṃ ca nivedite nyāyyaṃ sma saha vaidehyā draṣṭuṃ tau pārthivātmajau
english: "Since the mission has gone thus far and has been reported to you all, it is fitting that we now see those two princes together with Vaidehī."

sanskrit: aham eko 'pi paryāptaḥ sarākṣasagaṇāṃ purīm tāṃ laṅkāṃ tarasā hantuṃ rāvaṇaṃ ca mahābalam
english: "I alone am sufficient to destroy by force that city of Laṅkā with all its companies of rākṣasas, and Rāvaṇa the mighty as well."

sanskrit: kiṃ punaḥ sahito vīrair balavadbhiḥ kṛtātmabhiḥ kṛtāstraiḥ plavagaiḥ śaktair bhavadbhir vijayaiṣibhiḥ
english: "How much more so when accompanied by heroes — powerful, self-disciplined, skilled in weapons, capable vānara warriors such as yourselves, who are intent on victory!"

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu rāvaṇaṃ yuddhe sasainyaṃ sapuraḥsaram saputraṃ vidhamiṣyāmi sahodarayutaṃ yudhi
english: "I shall scatter Rāvaṇa in battle together with his army, his vanguard, his sons, and his brothers in arms."

sanskrit: brāhmam aindraṃ ca raudraṃ ca vāyavyaṃ vāruṇaṃ tathā yadi śakrajito 'strāṇi durnirīkṣyāṇi saṃyuge tāny ahaṃ vidhamiṣyāmi nihaniṣyāmi rākṣasān
english: "Even if Indrajit deploys his terrible divine weapons in battle — those of Brahmā, Indra, Rudra, Vāyu, and Varuṇa — I shall repel them all and slay the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: bhavatām abhyanujñāto vikramo me ruṇaddhi tam
english: "With your approval, my valor shall check him."

sanskrit: mayātulā visṛṣṭā hi śailavṛṣṭir nirantarā devān api raṇe hanyāt kiṃ punas tān niśācarān
english: "An incomparable and unceasing rain of mountains hurled by me could slay even the gods in battle — what then of those night-roaming demons?"

sanskrit: sāgaro 'py atiyād velāṃ mandaraḥ pracaled api na jāmbavantaṃ samare kampayed arivāhinī
english: "Though the ocean should overstep its shores and Mount Mandara should be uprooted, no enemy host in battle could make Jāmbavān tremble."

sanskrit: sarvarākṣasasaṃghānāṃ rākṣasā ye ca pūrvakāḥ alam eko vināśāya vīro vāyusutaḥ kapiḥ
english: "The heroic vānara, son of Vāyu — he alone is sufficient for the destruction of all the hosts of rākṣasas, and of the ancient rākṣasas as well."

sanskrit: panasasyoruvegena nīlasya ca mahātmanaḥ mandaro 'py avaśīryeta kiṃ punar yudhi rākṣasāḥ
english: "At the tremendous onslaught of Panasa and the great-souled Nīla, even Mount Mandara would be shattered to pieces — what then of the rākṣasas in battle?"

sanskrit: sadevāsurayuddheṣu gandharvoragapakṣiṣu maindasya pratiyoddhāraṃ śaṃsata dvividasya vā
english: "Name a match for Mainda or Dvivida in battles involving gods, asuras, gandharvas, serpents, or birds — you cannot."

sanskrit: aśviputrau mahāvegāv etau plavagasattamau pitāmahavarotsekāt paramaṃ darpam āsthitau
english: "These two best of vānaras, sons of the Aśvins, are of tremendous speed; filled with supreme pride born of the boon granted by the Grandfather."

sanskrit: aśvinor mānanārthaṃ hi sarvalokapitāmahaḥ sarvāvadhyatvam atulam anayor dattavān purā
english: "For the sake of honoring the Aśvins, the Grandfather of all worlds long ago bestowed upon these two an incomparable immunity from death."

sanskrit: varotsekena mattau ca pramathya mahatīṃ camūm surāṇām amṛtaṃ vīrau pītavantau plavaṃgamau
english: "Intoxicated by the pride of that boon, these two heroic vānaras once overpowered the great army of the gods and drank the immortal nectar."

sanskrit: etāv eva hi saṃkruddhau savājirathakuñjarām laṅkāṃ nāśayituṃ śaktau sarve tiṣṭhantu vānarāḥ
english: "These two alone, when roused to fury, are capable of destroying Laṅkā with all her horses, chariots, and elephants — let the other vānaras stand aside."

sanskrit: ayuktaṃ tu vinā devīṃ dṛṣṭabadbhiḥ plavaṃgamāḥ samīpaṃ gantum asmābhī rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "Yet it would be improper for us vānaras — who have seen the goddess but not brought her — to go into the presence of the great-souled Rāghava without her."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭā devī na cānītā iti tatra nivedanam ayuktam iva paśyāmi bhavadbhiḥ khyātavikramaiḥ
english: "To report there merely that 'the goddess was seen but not brought back' — this seems to me improper for you, whose valor is renowned."

sanskrit: na hi vaḥ plavate kaś cin nāpi kaś cit parākrame tulyaḥ sāmaradaityeṣu lokeṣu harisattamāḥ
english: "Among you, best of vānaras, none is your equal in leaping and none is your equal in valor throughout the worlds, including among gods and asuras."

sanskrit: teṣv evaṃ hatavīreṣu rākṣaseṣu hanūmatā kim anyad atra kartavyaṃ gṛhītvā yāma jānakīm
english: "Since the rākṣasa heroes have already been slain thus by Hanūmān, what else remains to be done here? Let us take Jānakī and depart."

sanskrit: tam evaṃ kṛtasaṃkalpaṃ jāmbavān harisattamaḥ uvāca paramaprīto vākyam arthavad arthavit
english: Jāmbavān, best of monkeys and one who knows the meaning of things, spoke with great delight to Aṅgada who had thus resolved, speaking words full of purpose.

sanskrit: na tāvad eṣā matir akṣamā no yathā bhavān paśyati rājaputra yathā tu rāmasya matir niviṣṭā tathā bhavān paśyatu kāryasiddhim
english: "This resolve is not incapable — as you see it, O prince. But let your gaze be fixed on the accomplishment of the mission in accordance with the will of Rāma."

sanskrit: tato jāmbavato vākyam agṛhṇanta vanaukasaḥ aṅgadapramukhā vīrā hanūmāṃś ca mahākapiḥ
english: Then the forest-dwellers — the heroes headed by Aṅgada and the great monkey Hanūmān — accepted the words of Jāmbavān.

sanskrit: prītimantas tataḥ sarve vāyuputrapuraḥsarāḥ mahendrāgraṃ parityajya pupluvuḥ plavagarṣabhāḥ
english: Then all of them, filled with joy and with Vāyu's son going before them, the foremost of vānaras leaped away, departing from the summit of Mount Mahendra.

sanskrit: merumandarasaṃkāśā mattā iva mahāgajāḥ chādayanta ivākāśaṃ mahākāyā mahābalāḥ
english: Like Meru and Mandara in their aspect, like great elephants in rut, massive in body and immense in strength, they seemed to cover the sky as they flew.

sanskrit: sabhājyamānaṃ bhūtais tam ātmavantaṃ mahābalam hanūmantaṃ mahāvegaṃ vahanta iva dṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: The beings of the air seemed to carry Hanūmān — honored by them, self-possessed, mighty in strength, and swift in his course — upon their very gazes.

sanskrit: rāghave cārthanirvṛttiṃ bhartuś ca paramaṃ yaśaḥ samādhāya samṛddhārthāḥ karmasiddhibhir unnatāḥ
english: Having secured the accomplishment of Rāghava's purpose and supreme glory for their master, they flew onward — their mission fulfilled, elevated by the success of their deeds.

sanskrit: priyākhyānonmukhāḥ sarve sarve yuddhābhinandinaḥ sarve rāmapratīkāre niścitārthā manasvinaḥ
english: All of them were eager to bring glad tidings; all delighted in the prospect of battle; all were resolute in purpose regarding vengeance for Rāma — stout-hearted warriors.

sanskrit: plavamānāḥ kham āplutya tatas te kānanaukṣakaḥ nandanopamam āsedur vanaṃ drumalatāyutam
english: Leaping through the sky, those forest-dwellers arrived at a grove filled with trees and creepers that resembled Nandana, the garden of the gods.

sanskrit: yat tan madhuvanaṃ nāma sugrīvasyābhirakṣitam adhṛṣyaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvabhūtamanoharam
english: This was the Madhuvana — the Honey Grove — so named, guarded and protected by Sugrīva, unapproachable by all creatures, yet delightful to the hearts of all.

sanskrit: yad rakṣati mahāvīryaḥ sadā dadhimukhaḥ kapiḥ mātulaḥ kapimukhyasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
english: It was ever guarded by the great and mighty monkey Dadhimukha — the maternal uncle of the great-souled Sugrīva, chief of the monkeys.

sanskrit: te tad vanam upāgamya babhūvuḥ paramotkaṭāḥ vānarā vānarendrasya manaḥkāntatamaṃ mahat
english: Arriving at that vast and most beloved grove of the lord of monkeys, the vānaras became supremely exuberant.

sanskrit: tatas te vānarā hṛṣṭā dṛṣṭvā madhuvanaṃ mahat kumāram abhyayācanta madhūni madhupiṅgalāḥ
english: Then the vānaras, honey-tawny and joyful at seeing the great Madhuvana, approached the young prince Aṅgada and begged him for the honey.

sanskrit: tataḥ kumāras tān vṛddhāñ jāmbavatpramukhān kapīn anumānya dadau teṣāṃ nisargaṃ madhubhakṣaṇe
english: Then the young prince, having obtained the consent of the elder monkeys headed by Jāmbavān, gave them freedom to partake of the honey.

sanskrit: tataś cānumatāḥ sarve saṃprahṛṣṭā vanaukasaḥ muditāś ca tatas te ca pranṛtyanti tatas tataḥ
english: And so, with permission given, all the forest-dwellers were overwhelmed with joy; delighted, they began to dance here and there.

sanskrit: gāyanti ke cit praṇamanti ke cin nṛtyanti ke cit prahasanti ke cit patanti ke cid vicaranti ke cit plavanti ke cit pralapanti ke cit
english: Some sang; some bowed down; some danced; some laughed loudly; some tumbled and rolled; some wandered about; some leaped; some chattered away.

sanskrit: parasparaṃ ke cid upāśrayante parasparaṃ ke cid atibruvante drumād drumaṃ ke cid abhiplavante kṣitau nagāgrān nipatanti ke cit
english: Some leaned upon one another; some boasted against each other; some leaped from tree to tree; some fell from the treetops to the ground.

sanskrit: mahītalāt ke cid udīrṇavegā mahādrumāgrāṇy abhisaṃpatante gāyantam anyaḥ prahasann upaiti hasantam anyaḥ prahasann upaiti
english: Some, rising with great speed from the ground, flew up to the tops of great trees; one who was singing approached another laughing, and another laughing approached one who laughed.

sanskrit: rudantam anyaḥ prarudann upaiti nudantam anyaḥ praṇudann upaiti samākulaṃ tat kapisainyam āsīn madhuprapānotkaṭa sattvaceṣṭam na cātra kaś cin na babhūva matto na cātra kaś cin na babhūva tṛpto
english: One who was weeping approached another weeping; one who was shoving another came and shoved him back. The monkey army was utterly in chaos, the behavior of every creature intoxicated by drinking honey. Not one among them was not drunk; not one among them was not satiated.

sanskrit: tato vanaṃ tat paribhakṣyamāṇaṃ drumāṃś ca vidhvaṃsitapatrapuṣpān samīkṣya kopād dadhivaktranāmā nivārayām āsa kapiḥ kapīṃs tān
english: Then, seeing the grove being plundered and the trees stripped of their leaves and blossoms, the monkey named Dadhimukha, in his fury, tried to restrain those monkeys.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ pravṛddhaiḥ paribhartsyamāno vanasya goptā harivīravṛddhaḥ cakāra bhūyo matim ugratejā vanasya rakṣāṃ prati vānarebhyaḥ
english: Threatened by those bold and spirited monkeys, the grove's guardian — elder among the heroic vānaras and fierce in his energy — resolved once more to defend the forest against the monkeys.

sanskrit: uvāca kāṃś cit paruṣāṇi dhṛṣṭam asaktam anyāṃś ca talair jaghāna sametya kaiś cit kalahaṃ cakāra tathaiva sāmnopajagāma kāṃś cit
english: He spoke harsh words to some boldly and without restraint; he struck others with his palms; he came to blows with still others; and to yet others he approached with conciliation.

sanskrit: sa tair madāc cāprativārya vegair balāc ca tenāprativāryamāṇaiḥ pradharṣitas tyaktabhayaiḥ sametya prakṛṣyate cāpy anavekṣya doṣam
english: But he was overpowered by those whose onslaught could not be checked for the force of their intoxication, and who themselves could not be stopped — fearless, they came upon him heedless of any fault, and dragged him about.

sanskrit: nakhais tudanto daśanair daśantas talaiś ca pādaiś ca samāpnuvantaḥ madāt kapiṃ taṃ kapayaḥ samagrā mahāvanaṃ nirviṣayaṃ ca cakruḥ
english: Stabbing him with their nails, biting him with their teeth, pummeling him with their palms and feet, all the monkeys together, in their drunken state, laid that guardian monkey low and left the great grove utterly ravaged.

sanskrit: tān uvāca hariśreṣṭho hanūmān vānararṣabhaḥ avyagramanaso yūyaṃ madhu sevata vānarāḥ
english: Hanūmān, best of monkeys and foremost bull among vānaras, spoke to them: "With minds undisturbed, partake freely of the honey, O monkeys."

sanskrit: śrutvā hanumato vākyaṃ harīṇāṃ pravaro 'ṅgadaḥ pratyuvāca prasannātmā pibantu harayo madhu
english: Hearing Hanūmān's words, Aṅgada — foremost among monkeys — replied with a clear and cheerful heart: "Let the monkeys drink honey."

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ kṛtakāryasya vākyaṃ hanumato mayā akāryam api kartavyaṃ kim aṅga punar īdṛśam
english: "The word of Hanūmān — one who has accomplished his mission — must of necessity be honored by me. Even what might otherwise be improper must be done; how much more so a matter such as this."

sanskrit: andagasya mukhāc chrutvā vacanaṃ vānararṣabhāḥ sādhu sādhv iti saṃhṛṣṭā vānarāḥ pratyapūjayan
english: Hearing those words from the mouth of Aṅgada, the bull-like vānaras responded with joyful acclamation, crying "Excellent! Excellent!" in his honor.

sanskrit: pūjayitvāṅgadaṃ sarve vānarā vānararṣabham jagmur madhuvanaṃ yatra nadīvega iva drutam
english: Having honored Aṅgada, that bull among vānaras, all the monkeys rushed toward the Madhuvana swift as the current of a river.

sanskrit: te prahṛṣṭā madhuvanaṃ pālān ākramya vīryataḥ atisargāc ca paṭavo dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca maithilīm
english: Elated — they who had seen and heard of Maithilī — and given free rein, those capable warriors overpowered the keepers of the Madhuvana by force.

sanskrit: utpatya ca tataḥ sarve vanapālān samāgatāḥ tāḍayanti sma śataśaḥ saktān madhuvane tadā
english: Then they all leaped up and rushed at the grove-keepers who had assembled, striking them by the hundreds as they stood their ground in the Madhuvana.

sanskrit: madhūni droṇamātrāṇi bahubhiḥ parigṛhya te ghnanti sma sahitāḥ sarve bhakṣayanti tathāpare
english: Taking up great vessels of honey — droṇa-measures full — they struck one another; others consumed it together in great quantities.

sanskrit: ke cit pītvāpavidhyanti madhūni madhupiṅgalāḥ madhūcciṣṭena ke cic ca jaghnur anyonyam utkaṭāḥ
english: Some honey-tawny monkeys, having drunk their fill, tossed the honey aside; others, intoxicated and unruly, pelted each other with the honeycomb leavings.

sanskrit: apare vṛkṣamūleṣu śākhāṃ gṛhya vyavasthitaḥ atyarthaṃ ca madaglānāḥ parṇāny āstīrya śerate
english: Others sat at the roots of trees clutching branches, and then, overcome to excess by the stupor of intoxication, spread leaves and lay down to sleep.

sanskrit: unmattabhūtāḥ plavagā madhumattāś ca hṛṣṭavat kṣipanty api tathānyonyaṃ skhalanty api tathāpare
english: The vānaras, like mad creatures and drunk with honey, flung themselves joyfully at one another, and still others stumbled and reeled about.

sanskrit: ke cit kṣveḍān prakurvanti ke cit kūjanti hṛṣṭavat harayo madhunā mattāḥ ke cit suptā mahītale
english: Some uttered wild shrieks; some cooed in delight; the monkeys drunk on honey lay stretched out asleep on the ground.

sanskrit: ye 'py atra madhupālāḥ syuḥ preṣyā dadhimukhasya tu te 'pi tair vānarair bhīmaiḥ pratiṣiddhā diśo gatāḥ
english: Even the honey-keepers who were servants of Dadhimukha were driven back by those fearsome monkeys and fled in all directions.

sanskrit: jānubhiś ca prakṛṣṭāś ca devamārgaṃ ca darśitāḥ abruvan paramodvignā gatvā dadhimukhaṃ vacaḥ
english: Dragged by the knees, shown the sky, and filled with great anguish, they went and spoke these words to Dadhimukha.

sanskrit: hanūmatā dattavarair hataṃ madhuvanaṃ balāt vayaṃ ca jānubhiḥ kṛṣṭā devamārgaṃ ca darśitāḥ
english: "The Madhuvana has been destroyed by force by those given leave by Hanūmān. We ourselves were dragged by the knees and shown the sky."

sanskrit: tato dadhimukhaḥ kruddho vanapas tatra vānaraḥ hataṃ madhuvanaṃ śrutvā sāntvayām āsa tān harīn
english: Then Dadhimukha the grove-warden, enraged upon hearing that the Madhuvana had been laid waste, pacified those monkeys who had come to him.

sanskrit: etāgacchata gacchāmo vānarān atidarpitān balenāvārayiṣyāmo madhu bhakṣayato vayam
english: "Come, let us go! We shall restrain by force those arrogant monkeys who are consuming the honey."

sanskrit: śrutvā dadhimukhasyedaṃ vacanaṃ vānararṣabhāḥ punar vīrā madhuvanaṃ tenaiva sahitā yayuḥ
english: Hearing these words of Dadhimukha, those heroic bull-like vānaras went once more to the Madhuvana, together with him.

sanskrit: madhye caiṣāṃ dadhimukhaḥ pragṛhya sumahātarum samabhyadhāvad vegenā te ca sarve plavaṃgamāḥ
english: Dadhimukha, in the midst of them and seizing an immense tree, rushed forward swiftly — and all the other vānaras did likewise.

sanskrit: te śilāḥ pādapāṃś cāpi pāṣāṇāṃś cāpi vānarāḥ gṛhītvābhyāgaman kruddhā yatra te kapikuñjarāḥ
english: Those monkeys, taking up rocks, trees, and boulders in their anger, came charging toward where the great elephant-like monkeys were.

sanskrit: te svāmivacanaṃ vīrā hṛdayeṣv avasajya tat tvarayā hy abhyadhāvanta sālatālaśilāyudhāḥ
english: Those heroes, fixing their master's command in their hearts, rushed forward swiftly, armed with śāla trees, palmyra palms, and rocks.

sanskrit: vṛkṣasthāṃś ca talasthāṃś ca vānarān baladarpitān abhyakrāmanta te vīrāḥ pālās tatra sahasraśaḥ
english: The grove-guardian warriors, by the thousands, fell upon the monkeys — those perched in trees and those standing on the ground — who were arrogant in their strength.

sanskrit: atha dṛṣṭvā dadhimukhaṃ kruddhaṃ vānarapuṃgavāḥ abhyadhāvanta vegena hanūmatpramukhās tadā
english: Then, seeing Dadhimukha enraged, the bull-like vānaras led by Hanūmān charged at him with great speed.

sanskrit: taṃ savṛkṣaṃ mahābāhum āpatantaṃ mahābalam taṃ āryakaṃ prāharat tatra bāhubhyāṃ kupito 'ṅgadaḥ
english: As that great-armed and mighty one came rushing forward with his tree, the furious Aṅgada there struck that elder with both arms.

sanskrit: madāndhaś a na vedainam āryako 'yaṃ mameti saḥ athainaṃ niṣpipeṣāśu vegavad vasudhātale
english: Blinded by intoxication, he did not recognize that this was his respected elder; swiftly and with great force he slammed him hard into the ground.

sanskrit: sa bhagnabāhur vimukho vihvalaḥ śoṇitokṣitaḥ mumoha sahasā vīro muhūrtaṃ kapikuñjaraḥ
english: With his arm broken, turning away, overwhelmed and drenched in blood, that heroic elephant among monkeys instantly fell senseless for a moment.

sanskrit: sa kathaṃ cid vimuktas tair vānarair vānararṣabhaḥ uvācaikāntam āgamya bhṛtyāṃs tān samupāgatān
english: That bull among vānaras somehow freed himself from those monkeys, withdrew to one side, and spoke to those servants who had come to him.

sanskrit: ete tiṣṭhantu gacchāmo bhartā no yatra vānaraḥ sugrīvo vipulagrīvaḥ saha rāmeṇa tiṣṭhati
english: "Let these ones stay here; we shall go to where our master, the broad-necked vānara Sugrīva, stands together with Rāma."

sanskrit: sarvaṃ caivāṅgade doṣaṃ śrāvayiṣyāmi pārthiva amarṣī vacanaṃ śrutvā ghātayiṣyati vānarān
english: "I shall report all of Aṅgada's transgressions to the king. He, the impatient one, upon hearing the words, will have the monkeys put to death."

sanskrit: iṣṭaṃ madhuvanaṃ hy etat sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ pitṛpaitāmahaṃ divyaṃ devair api durāsadam
english: "For this Madhuvana is the beloved grove of the great-souled Sugrīva — inherited from fathers and grandfathers, divine, and unapproachable even by the gods."

sanskrit: sa vānarān imān sarvān madhulubdhān gatāyuṣaḥ ghātayiṣyati daṇḍena sugrīvaḥ sasuhṛjjanān
english: "Sugrīva will punish and put to death all these monkeys — greedy for honey, their lives now forfeit — along with their companions."

sanskrit: vadhyā hy ete durātmāno nṛpājñā paribhāvinaḥ amarṣaprabhavo roṣaḥ saphalo no bhaviṣyati
english: "These wicked ones who have disregarded the king's command are fit for death. The anger born of our outrage shall bear fruit."

sanskrit: evam uktvā dadhimukho vanapālān mahābalaḥ jagāma sahasotpatya vanapālaiḥ samanvitaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the mighty Dadhimukha, together with the grove-keepers, leaped up at once and departed.

sanskrit: nimeṣāntaramātreṇa sa hi prāpto vanālayaḥ sahasrāṃśusuto dhīmān sugrīvo yatra vānaraḥ
english: In no more than the twinkling of an eye, that forest-dweller arrived at the place where the wise Sugrīva — son of the Sun of a thousand rays — stood.

sanskrit: rāmaṃ ca lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva dṛṣṭvā sugrīvam eva ca samapratiṣṭhāṃ jagatīm ākāśān nipapāta ha
english: Seeing Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and Sugrīva himself, he descended from the sky and alighted on the level ground.

sanskrit: sa nipatya mahāvīryaḥ sarvais taiḥ parivāritaḥ harir dadhimukhaḥ pālaiḥ pālānāṃ parameśvaraḥ
english: Having landed, that great and mighty monkey Dadhimukha, supreme lord of the grove-keepers, was surrounded by all of those keepers.

sanskrit: sa dīnavadano bhūtvā kṛtvā śirasi cāñjalim sugrīvasya śubhau mūrdhnā caraṇau pratyapīḍayat
english: With a look of misery on his face and his joined hands raised to his head, he pressed his forehead to the auspicious feet of Sugrīva.
